rows.practice: directs an original research project, sets unfamiliar artefacts against established readings and builds a systematic critique of how museums, galleries and heritage display art
rows.knowledge: how the discipline's methods have unsettled received readings of art and design and where the field sits within wider social and political life
rows.identity: a self-aware scholar of visual culture who judges own academic strengths and weaknesses and chooses between intellectual approaches with care

digest.definition: Studies artefacts as visual and material culture in every medium, from painting, sculpture and buildings to applied arts, performance, photography, film, social media and games, past and present
distinctiveFeatures: Studies artefacts as visual and material culture in every medium, from painting, sculpture and buildings to applied arts, performance, photography, film, social media and games, past and present
Joins close description (formal, iconographic, semiotic, material, spatial or functional analysis) with critical study of context, making, patronage and use
Reads "art" and "design" as historical categories shaped by colonialism, the Enlightenment and modern institutions, and examines inequalities of power and histories pushed to the margins
Interdisciplinary by nature, drawing on archives, literary texts and scientific analysis across the arts, humanities and sciences
Display is part of the subject: museums, galleries, heritage sites and digital display shape how artefacts are received, and many partner with courses
Object-based learning and visual and material literacy are its signature skills, built through study visits, collections and handling
Taught as single honours and as a component of many other degrees, among them fine art, design, architecture, heritage, curating and media

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: the subject examines power, class, race, gender, sexuality and health in artefacts, recentres marginalised voices, questions Eurocentric narratives and object provenance, and ties inclusive environments to the Equality Act and partnership practice (D1, 1.7, 1.10 to 1.12, 2.16); inclusive interpretation is a typical generic skill (4.4)
accessible teaching and assessment, hybrid delivery and reasonable adjustment under equality law; no prerequisites and portfolio entry; assessment inclusive by design (D1, 1.13 to 1.15, 3.13)

artefacts as vehicles for the UN goals; the environmental cost of making, conserving, travelling to and digitising artefacts; environmental context is part of the threshold skill of situating artefacts (D1, 1.16 to 1.18; 4.4)

the cultural economy and art markets, experiential and partnership learning, curatorial and public programming tasks, and graduate routes into museums, heritage and creative industries (D1, 1.19 to 1.21, 2.17)

guidance and disclosure of use, questions of authorship and creativity, critical AI fluency, new assessment forms and concerns over bias and energy use (D1, 1.22 to 1.26, 3.12); ethical use is a transferable skill (4.5)

transferable.text: You should be able to explain what you know or argue a case so others can follow it, writing English accurately.
You should be able to work well with others as part of a team.
You should be able to research and study well when your learning is guided and structured.
You should be able to understand and join today's debates about culture and society, such as those on inequality and sustainability.
You should be able to use digital tools, including generative AI used ethically, to research, choose and share information.
You should be able to work steadily, make sensible decisions and hand in assessments on time.
You should be able to take responsibility for your own work and understand what academic integrity means for it.
You should be able to reflect on how you are doing and use feedback to develop your thinking and improve your work.
You should be able to spot and question the values and ethics beneath culture, society and your own choices.
You should be able to show some awareness that what we know is uncertain, open to more than one reading and limited.

statements.about: course design for progression across years
statements.paraphrase: Course design teams use institutional guidance and external reference points for specifications, outcomes, challenge and content; the design will consider how each year's content and teaching prepares every student to move on to harder problems.

forPractitioner.text: Use institutional guidance and external reference points to set outcomes and challenge; the design will need to show how each year's content, learning and teaching equips all students for more complex work the next year.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design teams; the student meets its effect in how the years build

statements.about: progression through the levels to the threshold
statements.paraphrase: A student will move up through the levels as each institution's rules set out, each level expected to build knowledge, expertise and experience towards the threshold (and any higher) subject and generic skills; this will usually mean passing and gaining credit for all learning and assessment, practical work included.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each level so that students will build towards the threshold skills listed for the award; progression usually depends on passing and earning credit for every part of the course, practical components included.

forBeneficiary.text: You will move up one level each year as your university's rules allow, building towards the skills your degree asks for; usually that means passing every part of the course, including practical work, and earning its credit.

statements.appliesTo: students taking HAAD in joint or combined degrees
statements.about: joint and combined degrees
statements.paraphrase: Students taking HAAD within a joint or combined degree, major and minor routes included, will reach the core of the subject and generic skills set out here and will add further skills from their other subject or subjects.

forPractitioner.text: In joint, combined and major/minor routes, design the HAAD share so that students will achieve the core subject-specific and generic skills of this statement, while their other subject adds its own.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study HAAD as part of a joint or combined degree, you will gain the core subject and general skills of the field and add others from your second subject.

statements.about: periodic review and the student voice
statements.paraphrase: Degree-awarding bodies and their partners routinely gather and analyse information and review courses periodically to suit their needs; the student voice will be considered as part of this.

forPractitioner.text: Your periodic course review, alone or with partners, will take account of what students say, alongside the data you routinely gather and analyse.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the degree-awarding body in course review

statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Externality is essential to UK quality assurance; providers will use external reviewers in periodic review for an independent view of proposed changes and to make sure threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: In periodic review you will bring in external reviewers, for an independent view on proposed changes and a check that threshold standards are met and content fits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in periodic review

statements.about: inclusive, accessible assessment design
statements.paraphrase: Assessment methods will be inclusive from the outset, and accessibility and inclusion will shape which forms of assessment are used.

forPractitioner.text: Design assessment to be inclusive from the start: accessibility and inclusion will decide which forms of assessment you use, rather than being added afterwards.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design assessment; the student meets its effect

statements.about: evidence above threshold; Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do far better than the minimum threshold; each provider decides how to evidence that achievement and should refer to Annex D of the Frameworks, which describes the four honours classes (1st, 2.1, 2.2, 3rd).

forPractitioner.text: To evidence achievement above threshold, you should use Annex D of the Frameworks, its descriptions of first, upper second, lower second and third-class honours, alongside your own method.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging and classifying achievement; the student meets it through marks and class

statements.about: competence standards and EHRC guidance
statements.paraphrase: The minimum threshold standards do not set universal competence standards; a provider that develops competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 may draw on the statement and PSRB requirements, and should follow the latest Equality and Human Rights Commission guidance.

forPractitioner.text: The threshold standards are not competence standards; if you set competence standards in a programme specification, inform them from this statement and any PSRB requirements, and you should follow the current Equality and Human Rights Commission guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in writing competence standards

statements.about: visual and material culture of more than one region or period
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can analyse and interpret the art and objects of at least two regions or periods.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates analyse and interpret artefacts from more than one region or period, so the curriculum spans at least two.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will analyse and interpret art, buildings and objects from at least two parts of the world or periods of history.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: arguments about the culture of more than one region or period
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will build and hold arguments about the visual and material culture of at least two regions or periods.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will construct and sustain arguments grounded in knowledge of artefacts from more than one region or period.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will build and keep up your own arguments about art and objects from at least two places or periods.

statements.about: materials and making techniques of artefacts
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can describe and remark on the materials and making techniques of artefacts in the cultures studied.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates describe how artefacts in the cultures they study were made and from what, and comment on those materials and techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will describe what artefacts were made from and how, and comment on those materials and methods.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: arguments from knowledge of materials and techniques
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will build and hold arguments from knowledge of how and from what the artefacts of the cultures studied were made.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will argue from a grasp of materials and making processes, not only describe them.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will use what you know about materials and making methods to build and sustain your own arguments.

statements.about: current debates and approaches in the discipline
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can keep up with the discipline's present debates and approaches.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates keep track of current debates and approaches in the discipline.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will keep up with the current debates and ways of working in your subject.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: sound knowledge of debates; accurate interpretive technique
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will show secure knowledge of the discipline's present debates and approaches and use its recognised methods of interpretation accurately.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will know current debates and approaches soundly and apply the discipline's established interpretive techniques with accuracy.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will know the current debates well and use the subject's recognised ways of interpreting artefacts accurately.

statements.about: some acquaintance with how the arts and heritage sectors work
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show some acquaintance with professional practice in the arts and cultural industries, such as museums, galleries and heritage.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates have some familiarity with how museums, galleries, heritage bodies and the creative industries work.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will know something of how museums, galleries, heritage sites and the creative industries work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: using professional practice to argue and solve problems
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will engage with professional practice in museums, galleries, heritage and the creative industries and draw on it to argue and solve problems.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will engage with professional practice across the arts, heritage and creative sectors and use it to build arguments and tackle problems.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will engage with how museums, galleries, heritage and creative organisations work and use that to make arguments and solve problems.

statements.about: how art, design and architecture shape cultures and identities
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can analyse how art, design and architecture help shape, and comment on, cultures and identities.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates analyse the part art, design and architecture play in forming cultures and identities, and how they mirror that formation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will analyse how art, design and buildings help to shape cultures and identities and respond to them.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: theory applied to art, culture and identity
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will apply theory to how art, design and architecture shape and reflect cultures and identities.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will bring theory to bear on the role of art, design and architecture in forming and reflecting cultures and identities.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will use theory to explain how art, design and buildings shape and mirror cultures and identities.

statements.about: basic observation and description in analysis
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can use basic observation and visual and material description when analysing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates bring basic skills of close looking and of describing artefacts' visual and material qualities into their analysis.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will look closely at artefacts and describe what you see and what they are made of as part of your analysis.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: observation and description put to interpretation and argument
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will use observation and description of visual and material qualities to interpret artefacts and develop arguments.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will deploy close observation and description to interpret artefacts and to elaborate arguments.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will use close looking and careful description to interpret artefacts and develop your arguments.

statements.about: placing artefacts in context, environmental included
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can place artefacts in fitting environmental, historical and cultural contexts.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates place artefacts in suitable environmental, historical and cultural contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will place artefacts in the right environmental, historical and cultural settings.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: context used to advance enquiry
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will place artefacts in fitting historical and cultural contexts so as to move enquiry in the discipline forward.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will use historical and cultural context to push enquiry in the discipline forward, not only to label artefacts.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will use the historical and cultural setting of artefacts to open up new questions in your subject.

statements.about: interdisciplinary evidence on current issues
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can use evidence of many kinds from across disciplines, such as images, texts, technical data and primary and secondary material, on current questions in the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates draw on evidence from several disciplines, visual, spoken, written and technical, original and secondary, in addressing current issues in the field.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will use evidence from different subjects and kinds of source, such as images, texts, technical data, original and secondary material, on current questions.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: finding and weighing interdisciplinary evidence
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will find, use and weigh evidence from many kinds of source across disciplines to advance enquiry in the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will locate and critically evaluate evidence from several disciplines themselves and use it to move enquiry forward.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will find evidence for yourself across many kinds of source, judge how good it is and use it to move your enquiry on.

statements.about: awareness of the discipline's methods and theories
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show awareness of the discipline's established methods, theories and approaches.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates are aware of the established methodologies, theories and approaches of the field.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will know the main methods, theories and approaches used in your subject.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: choosing and using fitting methods and theories
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will use suitable established methods, theories and approaches of the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will choose and deploy fitting methodologies, theories and approaches from the field.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will choose and use the right methods, theories and approaches for the task.

statements.about: relevant arguments backed by evidence
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show some ability to make relevant arguments and concepts backed by visual, written or other fitting evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show some capacity to build relevant arguments and ideas supported by suitable evidence, visual, textual or other.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will show some ability to make relevant arguments backed by images, texts or other suitable evidence.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: consistent, well-built, evidenced argument
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will consistently make coherent, well-organised, relevant arguments backed by fitting visual, written or other evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will consistently write arguments that hang together, are well organised and relevant, with suitable supporting evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will consistently make clear, well-organised and relevant arguments backed by good evidence.

statements.about: telling alternative arguments apart
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can tell alternative arguments and approaches apart.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates distinguish between alternative arguments and approaches.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will be able to tell different arguments and approaches apart.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: critical judgement between competing approaches
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will show critical judgement, weighing alternative arguments and engaging with rival approaches.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will exercise critical judgement, evaluating alternative arguments and engaging with competing approaches.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will judge competing arguments critically and engage with approaches that differ from your own.

statements.about: understandable communication in varied media
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can communicate understandably in various media, with visual aids where needed.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates communicate comprehensibly across different media, using visual aids when the task calls for them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will communicate clearly enough to be understood in different media, using images or other visual aids where they help.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: effective communication to expert and lay audiences
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will communicate effectively in various media to specialist and general audiences, with visual aids where needed.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will communicate effectively in a range of media for both expert and lay audiences, using visual aids as needed.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will communicate well in different media to experts and non-experts alike, using visual aids where they help.

statements.about: guided information gathering and basic research
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can gather information and carry out basic research with guidance and help.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates gather information and do basic research when guided and supported.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will gather information and do basic research with guidance and help.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: self-directed, verifiable research
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will carry out self-directed research, retrieving information effectively and verifiably, reviewing it critically and organising it for the task.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will direct their own research, finding information reliably and traceably, reviewing it critically and organising it to suit the task.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will lead your own research, finding information in ways others can check, reviewing it critically and organising it for the task.

statements.about: open-mindedness to the unfamiliar
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show open-mindedness, being open to artefacts, issues, values and ideas they have not met before.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates are open-minded: willing to take seriously artefacts, issues, values and ideas new to them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will be open-minded about artefacts, issues, values and ideas you have not met before.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: inclusive interpretation
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will show they can interpret inclusively, allowing for the ideas, contexts and structures from which different visual and material cultures emerged.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will interpret inclusively, taking account of the ideas, settings and structures behind diverse visual and material cultures.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will interpret artefacts inclusively, taking account of the ideas, settings and structures behind different cultures.

statements.about: values and ethics in culture and society
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, can identify the values and ethics that underlie culture and society.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates identify the values and ethics underlying culture and society.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will spot the values and ethics that lie beneath culture and society.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: examining values and ethics in culture and society
statements.paraphrase: At the typical level, will identify and also examine the values and ethics that underlie culture and society.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will go beyond naming the values and ethics beneath culture and society to examine them.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical standard, you will not only spot the values and ethics beneath culture and society but examine them.

statements.about: clear presentation in sound written English
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to put knowledge or a case so others can follow it, with technically sound written English.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to put knowledge or a case across understandably, writing English with sound technical accuracy.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to explain what you know or argue a case so others can follow it, writing English accurately.

statements.about: effective teamwork
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to collaborate well as a member of a team.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to collaborate effectively as members of a team.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to work well with others as part of a team.

statements.about: effective study where learning is guided
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to research and study well in a guided, structured setting.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to research and study well where the learning is guided and structured.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to research and study well when your learning is guided and structured.

statements.about: current debates on culture and society
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to value and take part in current debates on culture and society, such as those on inequality and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to appreciate and join contemporary debates about culture and society, for instance on inequality and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to understand and join today's debates about culture and society, such as those on inequality and sustainability.

statements.about: ethical use of digital tools and GenAI
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to use digital technologies, generative AI included and used ethically, to research, choose and convey information.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to use digital tools, including generative AI applied ethically, to research, select and share information.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to use digital tools, including generative AI used ethically, to research, choose and share information.

statements.about: diligence, decisions and deadlines
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to work conscientiously, make sound decisions and keep to assessment deadlines.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to work diligently, decide appropriately and keep to assessment deadlines.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to work steadily, make sensible decisions and hand in assessments on time.

statements.about: responsibility for own work; academic integrity
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to take responsibility for their work and understand what academic integrity asks of it.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to own their work and understand the questions of academic integrity it raises.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to take responsibility for your own work and understand what academic integrity means for it.

statements.about: reflection and use of feedback
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to reflect on their progress and use feedback well to develop intellectually and do better.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to reflect on their progress and use feedback to deepen their thinking and raise their performance.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to reflect on how you are doing and use feedback to develop your thinking and improve your work.

statements.about: values and ethics, personal as well as social
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to identify and examine the values and ethics beneath culture and society and in their own lives.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to identify and examine the values and ethics in culture, in society and in themselves.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to spot and question the values and ethics beneath culture, society and your own choices.

statements.about: awareness of uncertainty and the limits of knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to show some awareness that knowledge is uncertain, ambiguous and limited.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show some awareness of the uncertainty, ambiguity and limits that come with any knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show some awareness that what we know is uncertain, open to more than one reading and limited.

statements.about: refined visual literacy
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to show refined, subtle visual literacy.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically show sophisticated, nuanced visual literacy.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually be able to read images and objects with real subtlety and sophistication.

statements.about: systematic, critical work with texts, artefacts and theory
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to engage systematically and critically with texts, artefacts and the theories and methods for studying visual and material culture.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically work systematically and critically with texts and artefacts and with the theories and methods of the field.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually work systematically and critically with texts, objects and the theories and methods used to study them.

statements.about: how methods and research have unsettled received readings
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to show how the discipline's methods and research trends have unsettled earlier assumptions and readings of art, architecture or design.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically understand how methodological change and research trends have overturned received views and readings in the field.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually be able to explain how new methods and research have overturned older assumptions about art, architecture or design.

statements.about: unfamiliar material set against established ideas
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to use unfamiliar arguments and artefacts productively while engaging critically with well-known or established ideas.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically put unfamiliar arguments and artefacts to good use and question the field's established ideas.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually be able to make good use of unfamiliar arguments and objects while questioning the field's established ideas.

statements.about: the subject in its social and political setting
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to show advanced knowledge of how the discipline sits within wider social and political contexts.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically show advanced knowledge of the subject's place in wider social and political contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually know in depth how your subject connects with wider social and political questions.

statements.about: a critical approach to display and representation
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to develop a systematic, critical approach to how art is represented in museums, galleries and heritage.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically form a systematic, critically engaged view of how museums, galleries and heritage bodies represent art.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually have a systematic and critical way of looking at how museums, galleries and heritage sites present art.

statements.about: grounding in analysis, argument and expression
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to show thorough grounding in analysis, argument and expression.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically be comprehensively grounded in analysis, argument and expression.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually be thoroughly skilled in analysing, arguing and expressing your ideas.

statements.about: assembling and connecting sources
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to gather data from varied relevant primary and secondary sources and see the links between them.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically bring together data from a range of pertinent original and secondary sources and see how they connect.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually gather information from many original and secondary sources and see how they connect.

statements.about: self-knowledge and reflection
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to see where they are strong and weak academically and think about how they are performing and progressing.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically know their academic strengths and weak points and review how well they are performing and progressing.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually know where you are strong and weak academically and reflect on how you are getting on.

statements.about: relating approaches and choosing one
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to see how different intellectual approaches relate and pick the right one for a given case.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically identify how intellectual approaches relate and choose those suited to a particular case.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually see how different ways of thinking relate and choose the right one for each case.

statements.about: an original, self-directed research project
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to complete an original research project that they direct themselves.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically carry out an original, self-directed research project.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually carry out an original research project that you lead yourself.

statements.about: communication to expert and lay audiences
statements.paraphrase: Should typically be able to convey ideas and structured arguments effectively to expert and general audiences.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should typically put across ideas and well-built arguments effectively to both expert and lay audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you should usually explain ideas and well-built arguments clearly to experts and non-experts.
